title: Real-time card fraud scoring
tagline: Streaming point-in-time features, gradient-boosted scoring and cost-optimised approve/review/decline bands behind a FastAPI service.

highlights: One streaming feature engine for training and serving; tests prove online features equal batch features and that no future event leaks into a feature.
Time-based split with realistic chargeback delay: 16% of training fraud was still unlabelled at the cut-off.
Approve/review/decline bands chosen by minimising expected dollar loss under a review-capacity limit, then applied unchanged to later months.
Drift monitor: population PSI flags seasonal spend drift; fraud-only PSI catches an account-takeover tactic change that cut ATO recall from 69% to 33%.
FastAPI /score returns score, decision, reason codes and model version; trees are compiled to flat arrays for sub-millisecond online inference.
limitations: Synthetic data: fraud patterns are designed, so absolute scores flatter the model compared with a real portfolio.
Feature state lives in one process's memory; production needs a shared low-latency feature store and idempotent, ordered event ingestion.
Perturbation reason codes are a cheap approximation, not exact SHAP values.
